clinician.final_diagnosis: Multinodular goiter spontaneous hemorrhage confirmed by postoperative histopathology
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 63-year-old woman with ESRD on hemodialysis for 6 years and a 1-year history of multinodular goiter presented with acute 1-day onset of large neck swelling, hoarseness, and progressive dysphagia. Initial workup revealed normal coagulation and thyroid function. Ultrasonography demonstrated multiple thyroid nodules with a well-defined retrotracheal mass (E004). CT scan at 24 hours showed an enlarged, nonenhancing mass compressing the airway and esophagus, consistent with acute hemorrhage (E005). Given respiratory compromise, the patient underwent urgent partial thyroidectomy after intubation (E007). Postoperative imaging confirmed excision of the left thyroid lobe and hematoma (E009). The patient was extubated on postoperative day 4, discharged on day 10, and achieved complete resolution of compressive symptoms and hoarseness with normal calcium levels. One-month follow-up ultrasound showed no residual mass.
